articles.title: The Shallow Sky
articles.summary: This document outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) activity calendar for July and August 2012, including general meetings, solar observing events, astronomy classes, and star parties. It also features an article detailing personal observations and techniques used during the May 2012 annular eclipse and Venus transit, discussing phenomena like the Venusian aureole. The article concludes with a guide to celestial objects visible in July and highlights the SJAA telescope loaner program and the Golden State Star Party.

articles.title: The Last Month In Astronomy
articles.summary: The article recaps significant astronomy events from the past month, highlighting the successful launch of NASA's NuSTAR X-ray telescope on June 13, 2012, designed to provide much clearer images. It also reports the cancellation of the $119 million GEMS project due to budget overruns on June 7, 2012. Finally, it details observations of the rare Venus Transit across the Sun on June 5, 2012, including public viewing events and images from solar telescopes.

articles.title: Recent Astronomical News and Features
articles.summary: This article from July 2012's SJAA Ephemeris highlights several astronomical developments: the confirmed direct collision course of the Andromeda Galaxy with the Milky Way in 4 billion years; the discovery of volcanic, not biological, organic chemistry on Mars; and an annular solar eclipse observed in May 2012. It also covers the Herschel space observatory's finding of a massive galactic filament and NASA's new program loaning the GALEX space observatory to Caltech for continued operation.

articles.title: It Must Be Astronomical...
articles.summary: NASA's Astrophysics Division is making a rapid succession of groundbreaking astronomical discoveries, announcing numerous planetary systems, galaxy clusters, and cosmic phenomena monthly, driven by observatories like Hubble, Spitzer, Chandra, Fermi, and Kepler. Future missions such as the James Webb Space Telescope are poised to further expand our understanding of exoplanets, dark matter, galaxy evolution, and the early universe. This continuous stream of findings is guided by an ambitious research program focused on key priorities, while local astronomical associations also host educational 'star parties'.
